notes:
I don't have any notes for you yet. Nothing I tried got me to a single source page, and your rules say I can only report what the pages actually say.

My first attempt was to open four pages at once: Enduring Word on Daniel 11, Precept Austin's Daniel 11 commentary, the Bible Hub commentaries on Daniel 11:2, and the NET Bible notes. The pages may have come back, but my script couldn't read the results because of an error in my own code. When I tried again, the tool said I'd run out of web calls for this turn. My other tools can't go online, so I couldn't get to any source another way.

I could write these notes from what I already know about Daniel 11, but I won't. It would break your rule against filling gaps from my own knowledge, and I'd have no real page links to give you.

**Next time, if you ask me to carry on, I'll:**
1. Read the verse-by-verse sources first: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub and StudyLight. That gives the traditional reading of each verse.
2. Look for real differences between Protestant traditions, mainly on how far the prophecy reaches. Most of verses 1–20 are usually read as already fulfilled in the Persian, Greek and later Greek kingdoms. Verses 21–22 bring in a cruel king (traditionally Antiochus Epiphanes), whom some teachers also see as a picture of a future Antichrist. I'll compare Reformed, Baptist, Methodist, Pentecostal and Lutheran teachers on this.
3. Check other views: the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship (including the question of when Daniel was written), and New Advent, Catholic.com or OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings, such as Jerome's commentary on Daniel if I can find it on an allowed site.

Every point will have the page link it came from, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
